fact: A 2-hour plasma glucose of 200 mg/dL or higher during a 75 g oral glucose tolerance test meets the diagnostic criterion for diabetes, which must be confirmed by repeat testing in the absence of unequivocal hyperglycemia.
source: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee (2024), Standards of Care, Section 2

fact: A 2-hour plasma glucose between 140 and 199 mg/dL during an oral glucose tolerance test indicates impaired glucose tolerance (prediabetes), a state of elevated future diabetes risk.
source: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee (2024), Standards of Care, Section 2

fact: Fasting plasma glucose of 126 mg/dL or higher or HbA1c of 6.5% or higher are alternative diagnostic criteria; this dataset contains only the 2-hour OGTT value, so these criteria cannot be checked by the system.
source: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee (2024), Standards of Care, Section 2

fact: Overweight (BMI 25 or higher) and obesity (BMI 30 or higher) are major modifiable risk factors for type 2 diabetes; screening is recommended for adults with overweight or obesity.
source: US Preventive Services Task Force (2021), Screening for Prediabetes and Type 2 Diabetes

fact: Screening for prediabetes and type 2 diabetes is recommended for adults aged 35 to 70 years who have overweight or obesity; risk of type 2 diabetes increases with age.
source: US Preventive Services Task Force (2021), Screening for Prediabetes and Type 2 Diabetes

fact: A family history of diabetes in first-degree relatives increases type 2 diabetes risk; in this dataset the Diabetes Pedigree Function summarises family history as a single score.
source: Smith et al. (1988); Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (2024), Diabetes Risk Factors

fact: A history of gestational diabetes or delivering a baby over 9 pounds increases later type 2 diabetes risk; the dataset records number of pregnancies but not gestational diabetes history.
source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (2024), Diabetes Risk Factors

fact: Hypertension (blood pressure of 130/80 mmHg or higher) is commonly present alongside type 2 diabetes and is part of cardiometabolic risk assessment; the dataset contains diastolic pressure only.
source: Whelton et al. (2018), ACC/AHA Hypertension Guideline

fact: Elevated 2-hour serum insulin can reflect insulin resistance, but insulin values were missing (recorded as zero) for about half of the records in this dataset, so the feature is imputed and less reliable.
source: Smith et al. (1988); dataset audit in ihds/data.py

fact: The Pima Indians Diabetes Database contains only females aged 21 and over of Pima Indian heritage; risk estimates may not transfer to men, children or other populations without revalidation.
Clinical decision support output should be reviewable by the clinician, who must be able to see the basis of a recommendation and remains responsible for the final decision.
source: US Food and Drug Administration (2022), Clinical Decision Support Software Guidance

fact: Explainability in healthcare AI supports clinician trust, informed consent and accountability, and should be designed together with the clinical workflow.
source: Amann et al. (2020), BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making

fact: For people with prediabetes, structured lifestyle programmes targeting about 7% weight loss and 150 minutes of weekly physical activity reduce progression to type 2 diabetes; referral decisions belong to the clinician.
source: Diabetes Prevention Program Research Group (2002), New England Journal of Medicine

fact: Input data drift, such as a glucose meter calibration change or a different referral population, can silently degrade a deployed model, so distributions and performance should be monitored against a reference set.
source: Evidently AI (2024) documentation; Sculley et al. (2015)
